dispatchedRepresentationsForTarget(target, caller) — CALLER-AUTHORITY for UI instance selection: copies the caller's authenticated authority handle, instance registry, lexical dictionaries and active tags. This is a bounded display projection, not a claim that general callable dispatch or decider reads use the reader's account.

frameAccount(ctx) → authenticateAuthority(ctx._authority)?.accountId — CALLER-AUTHORITY. rights R3a's ownership coordinate is DERIVED from the caller's minted handle, never authored and never read from a context slot. A boot, harness or kernel frame authenticates to no account and therefore sees no account-owned dispatch row; an empty string is not an account. It is a SELECTION input and never a judgment input.

modules/decidable-membership.ts `dmNatives` → plain `nativeImpls` — a REGISTERED decider door whose natives take NO context parameter, so no caller authority can reach them. FRONTIER: its natives are not classified below, because the door cannot carry what they would be classified on. Measured to answer opposite the direct call under an account registry.

perform → authenticateAuthority(frame._authority) — CALLER-AUTHORITY. The reference monitor's own read, keyed on the handle in the caller's frame rather than on any context identity or process state. An absent or unminted handle refuses.

perform → table.judge(envelope, argued) — CALLER-AUTHORITY. Evaluates `authority:permits` under the registry's KERNEL FRAME, which carries no perform table, no spec registry and no block scope, so the judgment cannot itself reach a table-resident act. The envelope judged is the one authenticated from the caller's handle, never an ambient one. rights R2b: the ACT is canonicalised first, through the alias map of the table on the caller's own frame — registry-static data, not process state, and unreachable from a frame that carries no table.

realm-local, eight-entry LRU of serialized results for the two RECIPE_STAGE_BODIES. Key: body fnId, complete own-data argument encoding, harness dispatch-pool version, fixture generation and evaluator-hook generation. Computation uses the argument copy; a changed code state refuses the store. Active fixtures, unavailable code state or refused snapshots compute without reuse; representation-inspection suppression bypasses it. Result-copy/encoding refusal does not store; every hit decodes a fresh value. No entry leaves the realm. This is the existing SIDE-CONDITIONED recipe.card.stage-memo claim: the curated no-perform stages must depend only on those inputs. It does not certify reached native leaves; this classification records the process-global read, not a new purity proof.
the three audit refutation clause names (purity / totality / signature-honesty). A frozen literal set.

memoizes, per function-BODY object, whether the body contains an `ann` node (`json-logic.ts` `bodyReadsSourceFunction`); only then does named-body entry set the `_sourceFunction` coordinate that call-site typing resolves annotation names through (modules-as-values Phase 2d). A structural fact about the key. A NEGATIVE answer is cached only for a wholly frozen body graph (every registry body is deep-frozen, so it cannot change); an unfrozen body is rescanned and carries the coordinate, so a body that gains an annotation never runs it detached. A lost entry rescans. tcb-ledger `eval.scope.source-function`.

maps a closure-carried import FRAME object's identity to its first descriptor-validated frozen names/aliases snapshot (`json-logic.ts` `canonicalImportFrame`), or to the frame itself when all three objects are frozen. This pins lexical name bindings, not just a speed result: a live key keeps its first snapshot. `closureLexicalImports` validates the caller-data list before this lookup, and `sameImportFrame` now reuses the caller context only for literal frame identity, never for a mutable original whose snapshot it holds. The registered-function import-frame path is separate; see `eval.scope.import-snapshot` in the TCB ledger for the closure-carried condition.

the dynamic `type_def` constructor table, keyed on its evaluator-state owner — ordinary `dispatchEngineBodyWithDeciderCtx` `{...ctx}` copies still cannot see it (`chk.ctor.harness-copy`). `constructorTableStable` now refuses to certify against a context that has one. The narrow admitted reader-metadata fork explicitly preserves the existing root or lexical state owner through readerMetadataContextStateOwners.
a frozen literal set of evaluator op names, fixed at module load. No authority.

interns evaluator contexts across repeated module/callback transitions, keyed on the CONTEXT object (`json-logic.ts` `lexicalEvaluateContext`). It is the one row here a rights reader should look at twice, and it is sound: `lexicalAmbientMatches` compares EVERY enumerable ambient slot by identity before reuse, and `_authority` is such a slot — so a frame carrying a different authority forms a NEW family rather than reviving the previous one's interned context. Only the `_importStack` name binding and the `_sourceFunction` coordinate (modules-as-values Phase 2d, the lexical source of annotation names) are allowed to vary within a family.
the reserved pattern meta-keys ($tag/$bind/$guard). A frozen literal set fixed at module load.

declared binding metadata, keyed on interpreter-owned DataContext objects (`json-logic.ts` `invokeFunction` and `matchPattern`). A registered parameter carries its type and source-function ID; a scalar constructor-field binder carries the source-selected field type and exact captured registered Type owner identity. This is required metadata, not a cached verdict: `copyOwnDataContext` explicitly carries it into evaluator copies, pattern merges carry each binder's declaration, and `defineDataContextBinding` invalidates the shadowed name. Own-data lookup disambiguates only an ambiguous scalar Number, resolving the declaration through the current reader's call-site typing hooks or captured Type declaration frame before fresh Reprable selection. It carries no authority, selected method, membership result or projection. An arbitrary external DataContext copy does not inherit these private facts; preserving them across interpreter copies is part of the semantic projection boundary, not a claim that losing the entry only costs time.

required active ctx-native invocation metadata, keyed on the actual host EvaluateContext. It retains only the active host handler identity and frozen written/resolved/selected keys; the getter returns function-free keys only to that same handler. Nested calls restore the previous entry in finally and outer completion/throw deletes it. It is not a result cache and stores no authority, dispatch instance, verdict or reflection snapshot. Losing active metadata would lose alias provenance, so installation/restoration is a semantic obligation.
a pattern-plan CACHE keyed on context identity. A miss recomputes, so a lost entry costs time, not truth.

the bare-name routing snapshot, read on every bare-name resolution INCLUDING inside decider bodies. P1(a.18) re-keyed it from the context OBJECT onto the registry's own stable getter — the repair pattern this phase reuses — so a context copy no longer loses it.

private evaluator-frame aliases created by readerStateEvaluateContext for readerSourceMetadataEvaluateContext, authoringInvocationEvaluateContext and noPerformEvaluateContext, and by the equivalent lexical-frame fork. Each alias retains the exact preexisting dynamic type_def state owner while its ambient reader packet remains fresh. Keys and values are actual host EvaluateContext objects; packets and authored row identities cannot select an owner. No source lookup, selected instance, verdict, authority or grant is cached. Descriptor copying preserves the original frozen posture and AuthorityRef identity; ordinary context copies receive no alias automatically.

canonical-source Reprable.JsRuntime candidate-presence facts, keyed ONLY on an original or qualified engine-copied immutable RoutingTable snapshot (`json-logic.ts` `runtimeRepresentationInspectionPlan`). The private WeakMap transports the source's owner-name set and wildcard flag; it does not cache a selected method, membership verdict, authority, projection or reader callback result. Internal pooled facts use the fixed harness source in a no-perform frame. Exact canonical served hooks and absent fixture/dynamic-constructor posture gate hits; existing hook/fixture generations fence stores through execution and decoding. Custom hooks compute uncached. Unqualified caller tables are never cached; version changes supply a new snapshot. Every read checks the current lexical frames through source `representationProjectionFrameCandidate`, preserves general scopes as potential candidates, and runs complete selection with fresh visibility, account, priority and conflict checks before semantic inspection. A lost entry recomputes the same immutable snapshot fact; it does not detach a reader's authority or suppress a new frame candidate.
